faq.answer: Intense attunement does not prove one-to-one Nine. Affection, collaborative skill, translation, caregiving, or safety dependence may produce close coordination; examine preference provenance and access to refusal.
faq.question: Does intense attunement prove one-to-one Nine?

faq.answer: Preference merging should be compared across power by recording each choice before discussion, then checking money, housing, care, language, and exit access; agreement under costly refusal is not clean subtype evidence.
faq.question: How should preference merging be compared across power?

faq.answer: Evidence challenges a shared-identity hypothesis when the person keeps a separate plan, names disagreement before attuning, tolerates temporary distance, and reconnects without surrendering consent or preference.
faq.question: Which evidence challenges a shared-identity hypothesis?

sections.body_md: Ask what the person wanted before a close other expressed a plan, then observe whether the preference stays available during connection. Affection and compromise are ordinary and not subtype evidence.
sections.title: Track preference before attunement

sections.body_md: Use one decision where both people have money, exit, and speaking power, then compare a decision shaped by dependency. Agreement under unequal consequences cannot establish preference merging.
sections.title: Compare equal and unequal influence

sections.body_md: One-to-one instinct is a traditional attention comparison rather than evidence about bodily mechanisms, chemistry, or a universal pair-bond system. Consent and access to exit remain primary.
sections.title: Describe relational attention without mechanism

sections.body_md: A person may initiate contact, advocate strongly for the relationship, or enjoy intense shared activity while still losing track of a separate agenda in specific decisions.
sections.title: Allow intensity and visible initiative

sections.body_md: Translation duty, caregiving, disability assistance, migration status, financial dependence, abuse, housing insecurity, and cultural expectations may constrain separate choices.
sections.title: Control for care and coercion

sections.body_md: Confidence should fall when the person names a preference first, sustains a separate plan, tolerates temporary disconnection, refuses pressure, and reconnects without erasing the disagreement.
sections.title: Look for closeness with intact separateness

sections.body_md: Evidence from one subtype measure cannot turn relational attunement into a universal category across cultures. Observations must never excuse coercion or treat another person’s consent as typology data.
sections.title: Keep relational inference provisional

sections.body_md:
Duration: 4

Context: Over four days, choose one shared purchase, one social plan, and one disagreement with a close person where each party can state a preference.

Observable signal: Record each preference before discussion, money and exit access, first proposal, changes made, pressure cues, final agreement, and separate follow-through.

Page-specific signal: Compare attunement in an equal-power decision with agreement where housing, care, language, or finances make refusal costly.

Alternative explanation: Check affection, cultural compromise, translation, disability support, migration status, coercion, financial dependence, and actual safety.

Reflection prompt: Identify one close interaction where separateness improved trust, then revise the preference-merging hypothesis while preserving consent boundaries.

seo.description: Type Nine one-to-one is a traditional secondary hypothesis linking a core-Nine stability pattern with attunement, shared identity, intense connection, and difficulty locating a separate preference. It does not describe bodily mechanisms. Similar agreement can arise from care, language brokerage, disability support, financial dependence, coercion, or a realistic need for safety.
seo.title: Type Nine one-to-one: attunement and preference merging as a secondary hypothesis
